question.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

$$
f(0)=3,\,{f}^{′}(0)=2,\,g(0)=\frac{1}{2},\,{g}^{′}(0)=-1
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=0.$

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=0}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=0,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=0} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(0)g(0)-f(0){g}^{′}(0)}{(g(0))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot (\frac{1}{2})-3\cdot (-1)}{{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1+3}{\frac{1}{4}} \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$
